questions.q: A lid measures $31.4$ cm around and $10$ cm across. What is the distance around divided by the distance across?
questions.work: $31.4 \div 10 = 3.14$. For every circle, circumference $\div$ diameter is $\pi$, about $3.14$.

questions.q: A segment through the center of the circle is $34$ m long. How far is it from the center to the circle?
questions.work: A segment through the center is a diameter. Center to circle is a radius: $34 \div 2 = 17$.

questions.q: The largest possible circle is cut from a square card $18$ cm on a side. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.work: The circle is as wide as the card, so its diameter is $18$. The radius is half: $18 \div 2 = 9$.

questions.q: A circular track is $50$ m across. How far is $4$ laps around it? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: One lap is the circumference: $3.14 \cdot 50 = 157$. Then $157 \cdot 4 = 628$.

questions.q: The circumference of the circle is $15.7$ cm. Find the diameter. Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: $C = \pi d$, so $d = C \div \pi = 15.7 \div 3.14 = 5$.

questions.work: Diameter first: $62.8 \div 3.14 = 20$. The radius is half: $20 \div 2 = 10$.

questions.work: $C = \pi d$, so the diameter is $26$. The radius is half: $26 \div 2 = 13$.

questions.q: A rope $219.8$ m long fits exactly once around the edge of a circular pond. How far is it straight across the pond, through the center? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: The rope is the circumference, and straight across is the diameter: $219.8 \div 3.14 = 70$.

questions.work: The figure gives the diameter, so the radius is $8 \div 2 = 4$. Then $3.14 \cdot 4 \cdot 4 = 50.24$.

questions.work: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \cdot 6 \cdot 6 = 36\pi$. Exact means $\pi$ stays in the answer.

questions.q: Find the area of the half circle. Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: The radius is $12 \div 2 = 6$. A whole circle would be $3.14 \cdot 6 \cdot 6 = 113.04$, and half of that is $56.52$.

questions.q: One quarter of the circle is cut away. Find the shaded area. Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: The whole circle is $3.14 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 = 314$. Three quarters are left: $314 \div 4 \cdot 3 = 235.5$.

questions.q: A circular rug has a radius of $3$ ft. How much floor does it cover? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: Covering a surface is area: $3.14 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 = 28.26$.

questions.q: Ribbon is glued around the edge of a circular mirror that is $40$ cm across. How long is the ribbon? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: Around the edge is circumference: $3.14 \cdot 40 = 125.6$.

questions.q: A sprinkler waters all the lawn within $5$ m of it. How much lawn does it water? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: The lawn it reaches is a circle with radius $5$, and how much lawn is area: $3.14 \cdot 5 \cdot 5 = 78.5$.

questions.q: A pizza $20$ in. across is cut into $8$ equal slices. What is the area of one slice? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: The radius is $10$, so the whole pizza is $3.14 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 = 314$. One slice: $314 \div 8 = 39.25$.

questions.q: A circular garden is $10$ m across. Fencing to go around it costs \$6 per meter. What does the fence cost? Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
questions.work: A fence goes around, so find the circumference: $3.14 \cdot 10 = 31.4$ m. Then $31.4 \cdot 6 = 188.40$.

final.q: The edge of a circular pond is $94.2$ m long. Find the area of the pond's surface. Use $3.14$ for $\pi$.
final.work: Work back to the radius: $94.2 \div 3.14 = 30$ across, so $r = 15$. Then $A = 3.14 \cdot 15 \cdot 15 = 706.5$.
